title: Tighter bail: "two strikes, no bail" for repeat violent offenders
summary: The Libertarian Party says repeat violent offenders would be remanded with no exceptions, and that people charged with one serious offence would get bail only if the court is confident there is no risk.
excerpt: Two strikes, no bail. Repeat violent offenders are remanded — no exceptions.

title: Fast-track serious cases and assign case officers to victims
summary: The party proposes fixed timelines to fast-track serious criminal cases, a new supervised order with mandatory treatment and court reviews for repeat offenders, and a dedicated case officer for every victim of serious crime.
excerpt: Put victims at the centre. A dedicated case officer for every serious crime victim — informed, heard, not forgotten.

title: Fill more than 1,000 Victoria Police vacancies within two years
summary: The party says it would fill over 1,000 police vacancies within two years, funded in part by stopping the Suburban Rail Loop.
excerpt: Rebuild Victoria Police. Over 1,000 vacancies. Filled within two years. Treated as the emergency it is. Stop the SRL debt bomb to pay for police.

title: Legalise cannabis for adults
summary: The party would legalise cannabis for adults "with sensible rules", saying this would remove a black market it estimates at about $1 billion a year. It also proposes expanding heroin treatment options to reduce demand.
excerpt: The cannabis black market. Legalise for adults with sensible rules. Take roughly $1 billion a year away from criminal gangs.

title: Cut tobacco excise to target the illicit tobacco trade
summary: The party proposes cutting tobacco excise tax, which it links to the illicit tobacco market and related arson attacks; it also says vaping laws have created a black market.
excerpt: The tobacco black market. Cut excise tax. End the billion-dollar profit that’s driving arson attacks and murders across Victoria.

title: Legalise pepper spray for self-defence
summary: The party would legalise carrying pepper spray for self-defence and review Victoria's self-defence laws.
excerpt: Legalise pepper spray.

title: Introduce UK-style "Castle Law" for home self-defence
summary: The party would legislate home self-defence provisions based on UK "Castle law", under which only "grossly disproportionate" conduct by a householder would be prohibited.
excerpt: Our legislation will be based on United Kingdom law known as Castle law. This will mean you have special provisions around self-defence in your home, only prohibiting conduct that is "grossly disproportionate".

title: Royal Commission into the CFMEU
summary: The party says it would order a Royal Commission into the CFMEU in Victoria, as Queensland has done.
excerpt: CFMEU corruption cover-up. Queensland launched a Royal Commission. Victoria refused. We will order one — and follow the money.

title: Phase stamp duty down to zero
summary: The party would abolish stamp duty on property purchases, phasing it down to 0% as part of a 10-year tax reform program.
excerpt: We’ll phase stamp duty down to 0%—permanently. Buying a home will be cheaper.

title: Abolish the urban growth boundary and zoning restrictions
summary: The party proposes abolishing Melbourne's urban growth boundary, eliminating zoning restrictions, and legalising tiny homes, prefabricated housing and conversions, with protections retained against genuinely harmful noise and pollution.
excerpt: ABOLISH urban growth boundary - Let Melbourne grow naturally

title: Cancel the Suburban Rail Loop
summary: The party would cancel the Suburban Rail Loop, citing its projected cost and state debt; it acknowledges advice that cancelling contracts could require a payout of about $6 billion.
costing: Party cites an estimated $6 billion contract cancellation payout
excerpt: The Libertarian Party in government will cancel the Suburban Rail Loop.

title: Cut payroll tax by over 65% and scrap the emergency services levy
summary: The party proposes reducing payroll tax by more than 65% and abolishing the Emergency Services and Volunteers Fund levy, funding those services directly, with reforms phased over 10 years.
excerpt: We’ll slash payroll tax by over 65% to boost wages and help create jobs.

title: Cut public service administrative spending by 4% a year
summary: The party says its tax cuts would be funded by a 4% annual cut to bureaucratic spending, excluding frontline staff such as teachers, nurses, police and paramedics, and by stopping Suburban Rail Loop spending.
excerpt: A 4% cut to government bureaucrat spending each year.  That’s how we pay for tax cuts and chip away at debt—without gutting services – not touching teachers, nurses, police, paramedics etc

title: Constitutional limits: balanced budgets and a 15% spending cap
summary: The party proposes constitutional spending limits requiring balanced budgets and capping government spending at 15%, along with public tracking of spending and an end to what it calls secret slush funds.
excerpt: Cap spending at 15% - government can't grow bigger than the economy.

title: Restore $300,000 land tax threshold and abolish windfall gains tax
summary: The party would restore the land tax threshold to $300,000, abolish the Windfall Gains Tax, reverse COVID-era levies, and cut payroll tax rates while lifting the tax-free threshold.
excerpt: Land tax — restore the $300,000 threshold (the government cut it to $50,000).

title: Scrap the Social Procurement Framework and cut red tape
summary: The party would scrap the Social Procurement Framework for government contracts, require cost-benefit tests for new legislation, set net red-tape reduction targets and enforceable planning and permit timeframes.
excerpt: Scrap the Social Procurement Framework — no more locking Victorian businesses out of government contracts or letting activists pick who competes.

title: Legalise nuclear power and make net zero voluntary
summary: The party would repeal Victoria's nuclear power ban, make net zero voluntary rather than mandatory, allow exploration and extraction of coal, gas, oil and uranium, and scrap energy subsidies.
excerpt: Modern nuclear is safe, efficient, and clean. We must repeal the outdated ban and bring Victoria into the 21st century.

title: No new national parks; oppose duck-hunting bans
summary: The party opposes creating new national parks and opposes duck-hunting bans and shortened seasons without strong, transparent science, while proposing that public land be "open by default".
excerpt: No new national parks. We believe they bring more restrictions and more cost to taxpayers without clear environmental benefit.

title: Education vouchers so funding follows the student
summary: The party proposes education vouchers allowing parents to use public funding at the school of their choice, including for homeschooling families.
sourceTitle: FREE EDUCATION FROM THE MESS - Libertarians Victoria
excerpt: EDUCATION VOUCHERS - YOUR TAX DOLLARS FOLLOW YOUR CHILD

title: Repeal social cohesion and conversion-practices laws
summary: The party would repeal Victoria's social cohesion (anti-vilification) laws and the conversion-practices ban, while keeping coercion, force and harm to children illegal, and proposes a Bill of Rights in the state Constitution.
excerpt: Social Cohesion laws — repealed in full, day one.

title: Review of youth gender medical treatment
summary: The party supports a broad, systematic review of youth gender medical treatment similar to the UK Cass review, and prioritising parental involvement in decisions about gender-questioning children.
sourceTitle: Sex Based Rights Policy - Libertarians Victoria
excerpt: The Libertarian Party supports a broad and systematic review of youth gender medical treatment, similar to the UK Cass review.
